changes: NOTHING WAS CHANGED. This is not a transcription: the manufacturer serves this model as a text file, so it was frozen byte-for-byte under vendor/ and the whole file - model text and the vendor's own comment blocks - was appended below a header of our own. No parameter was removed (unlike models/jfet/lsk489.lib and models/bjt_pnp/ls350.lib, where mfg= had to be stripped because ngspice evaluates it as an expression and dies; this file has no mfg=), no value was rounded, reordered or 'corrected', and the model NAME was left exactly as served. Verifiable rather than asserted: diff <(grep -v '^\*' <vendor file>) <(grep -v '^\*' <this file>) is empty. One consequence worth knowing: the vendor file uses CRLF and our header uses LF, so the assembled file has MIXED line endings. That is deliberate - normalising the whole file rewrites the vendor bytes and breaks the diff above, silently. It happened once during L25 and only the diff caught it.
reason: T7 (ADR-016), NC-017. NPN half of the complementary Class A emitter follower that forms the output stage of the gain block (circuits/preamp/gain_block.py:367). ADR-016 had written that if the two MJE lacked a manufacturer model the output stage would be a TOPOLOGY change rather than a package swap; L24 found the model at onsemi's /download/models/lib/ path, so the output stage stands. The part stays, attributed to onsemi (OPN MJE15032G, Active).
notes: MIXED VERDICT - TWO POINTS OUTSIDE THE MANUFACTURER'S OWN DATASHEET (MJE15032/D, December 2024 Rev. 7), ngspice 47, set temp = 25. hFE at IC = 0.5 A, VCE = 5 V is 66.389 against a 70 MINIMUM: 5.1% short, recorded as NC-024. hFE 61.335 at 1.0 A (50 min) and 53.488 at 2.0 A (10 min) are inside. fT at IC = 500 mA, VCE = 10 V is 27.667 MHz against a 30 MHz MINIMUM: 7.8% short, recorded as NC-025 and NEW IN L25. The number changes from L24's 31.04 MHz because of the DEFINITION, which is the datasheet's own: Note 2 says 'fT = hfe ftest' and the test row gives ftest = 1.0 MHz, so fT is the gain-bandwidth product measured AT 1 MHz, not the |hfe| = 1 crossing (which gives 30.713 MHz and would clear the minimum). At 1 MHz this device is only ~2.6 octaves above its own beta pole, so the two definitions genuinely differ - and the manufacturer's minimum is written against the 1 MHz test. Bias verified: op prints IC = 5.000000e-01. Both deviations run in the PESSIMISTIC direction - less gain, less speed than the guaranteed part - which is the safe direction but not a known amount. Same shape as NC-013 on the LSK489 and NC-020 on the LS352. THE 2.0 A POINT CORRECTS L24, which recorded it as 'not reached': that was the extent of its base sweep, not a property of the model, which reaches IC = 6.8 A smoothly. THE MODEL WAS WRITTEN BY A CONTRACTOR AND THAT IS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN: its own header says 'Model Generated by MODPEX / Copyright(c) Symmetry Design Systems / Modeling services provided by Interface Technologies', 1 February 2004, PSpice format. A model the manufacturer DISTRIBUTES is what ADR-016 asks for; recording the author is part of what provenance is. The model is 22 years old and it is the newest thing onsemi publishes for the part. NO KF/AF, therefore NO 1/f noise - in this repo only models/jfet/lsk489.lib has flicker noise, which is why NC-004 does not close when the real models arrive. Any noise figure computed with this device is a floor without flicker and must say so next to the number.
